sections.overview: Phyllium bioculatum is a leaf insect in family Phylliidae; recent taxonomy places it in Pulchriphyllium.
sections.identification: Its flattened, leaf-like form provides camouflage among foliage.
sections.habitat: A Singapore record documents an individual at a secondary-forest edge; this does not establish its full habitat range.
sections.diet: The sources consulted do not establish its wild diet or food plants.
sections.behavior: Leaf insects resemble leaves, a form of camouflage documented in research on the group.
sections.reproduction: Its eggs have a distinctive fused-fin form, and researchers have measured how their surface adhesive works.
sections.ecology: The name has been used for a broader group: taxonomic work separated the Sri Lankan form agathyrsus as its own species.
sections.conservation: Available sources focus on taxonomy and biology and do not describe conservation threats.
